title: Remote Work and Auditors' Work-Life Balance: Disproportionate Impacts on Engagement Leaders
affiliations: University at Buffalo (SUNY) - School of Management, Temple University - Department of Accounting, Donald G. Costello College of Business at George Mason University and Georgia Southern University

detail.title: Remote Work and Auditors' Work-Life Balance: Disproportionate Impacts on Engagement Leaders
detail.abstract: We study how the abrupt transition to remote work during COVID-19 impacted the work-life balance of audit engagement leaders (i.e., managers and above) by examining audit-employee reviews on Glassdoor.com. We find general declines in auditors’ work-life balance, with engagement leaders experiencing the greatest decline. The disproportionate effect on engagement leaders’ work-life balance is concentrated in offices less equipped for transitioning to a remote-work environment (i.e., non-Big 4 offices and offices auditing clients with fewer foreign operations) and in offices serving more financially distressed clients. However, engagement leaders’ overall satisfaction and turnover intentions remain unchanged. Our findings offer insights into how remote work impacts auditors by highlighting the specific challenges faced by audit engagement leaders and provide a lens for viewing firms’ efforts to institute return-to-work policies. We provide suggestions for how accounting firms can respond to the decline in engagement leaders’ work-life balance.

affiliations: Advocate High Court

detail.title: Saudi Arabia: A Guide to its Trade Remedies Law
detail.abstract:
The global trading system, governed by the World Trade Organization (WTO), is founded on principles of liberalization and non-discrimination. However, it also provides member states with legal instruments to counteract injurious trade practices that distort competition. These instruments, known as trade remedies, are a critical component of modern trade policy, allowing countries to defend their domestic industries against unfair competition from abroad. 


This article introduces the legal and strategic context of trade remedies in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, a landscape defined by a recent and significant evolution from a regional framework to a robust national system.


The establishment of a national trade remedy framework marks a new era of maturity in Saudi Arabia's international trade policy. The system, anchored by the 2022 Law and administered by General Authority for Foreign Trade (GAFT), is robust, procedurally detailed, and aligned with the Kingdom's WTO commitments. Its dual operation alongside the GCC-wide system provides domestic industries with flexibility and a powerful, tailored tool to address injurious trade practices specific to the Saudi market.

detail.title: Monetary Policy Transmission and Inflation Dynamics in Post-Pandemic Oil-Dependent Economies: Evidence from Algeria
detail.abstract: This study presents an enhanced methodological approach to assess monetary policy efficacy in post-pandemic inflation dynamics, using Algeria as a case study. We employ a mixed-methods framework combining traditional econometrics with novel applications tailored to COVID-19 challenges in oil-dependent economies. Our approach integrates Vector Autoregression (VAR) modeling, Granger causality tests, impulse response functions, and variance decomposition analysis, supplemented by event study analysis. We introduce structural break tests and rolling window estimations to account for evolving economic relationships during the pandemic. The methodology incorporates exogenous variables such as COVID-19 cases and global commodity prices to control pandemic-specific effects. Applying this to Algerian data from 2018 to 2023, we provide insights into monetary policy transmission in a challenging environment. Our findings reveal the complex interplay between monetary tools, external shocks, and inflationary pressures, offering guidance for post-pandemic economic recovery in oil-dependent economies. Method details: Integration of pandemic-specific variables in VAR models for more accurate policy effectiveness assessment. Combined structural break analysis with rolling window estimations for dynamic view of changing economic relationships. Tailored event study framework accounting for unique policy interventions in oil-dependent economies during a pandemic.

detail.title: Could Carbon Tariff  Encourage Technology Transfer?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflict of interests to disclose.

detail.abstract: This paper argues that the introduction of a carbon tariff on dirty goods may influence the decision to transfer technology if consumers hold a strong preference for clean goods and dirty exports negatively affect the foreign environment. With carbon tariffs, dirty production becomes costly for the licensee. By transferring green technology, the licensor raises the licensee's marginal cost, replaces the dirty export market with clean goods, and expands the clean market, making technology transfer profitable for the licensor despite increased competition. The EU has introduced CBAM (Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism) as a carbon tariff on dirty imports, based on the assumption that such a tariff may incentivise technology transfer. Using a simple duopoly game between a clean domestic producer and a dirty exporter to explore several key findings. First, carbon tariffs on dirty exports can encourage technology transfer when the cross-border impact of dirty exports and the degree of foreign consumers' preference for clean goods are sufficiently high. Second, the licensee prefers only a fixed fee contract for green technology transfer. Third, the licensing incentive tends to rise with the introduction of a carbon tariff as switching to green technology becomes more profitable for the licensee. These 1 findings largely hold under Bertrand competition. However, technology transfer does not occur when bargaining power is shared, regardless of whether a carbon tariff is imposed or not. A key innovation of this paper is the inclusion of two parameters capturing the degree of consumer preference for clean goods and the adoption decision of green technology in the consumer utility function.

AI.tldr: 本文探讨了碳关税对绿色技术转移的影响，发现在消费者偏好清洁产品且污染出口对环境有负面影响时，碳关税能激励技术转移。通过双寡头博弈模型分析，发现碳关税使污染生产对受许可方成本更高，技术转移通过提升边际成本、替代污染出口市场并扩大清洁市场而变得有利可图。
AI.research_question: 碳关税如何影响绿色技术转移决策？
AI.motivation: 欧盟引入CBAM（碳边境调节机制）作为对污染进口的碳关税，基于此类关税可能激励技术转移的假设。
AI.theoretical_framework: 使用双寡头博弈模型，包含清洁国内生产商和污染出口商之间的竞争，创新性地在消费者效用函数中加入了消费者对清洁产品偏好程度和绿色技术采用决策两个参数。
AI.method: 简单的双寡头博弈分析，比较碳关税引入前后的技术转移决策。
AI.findings: 1) 当污染出口的跨境影响和外国消费者对清洁产品偏好足够高时，碳关税能鼓励技术转移；2) 受许可方偏好仅采用固定费用合同的绿色技术转移；3) 随着碳关税引入，受许可方转向绿色技术更有利可图，许可激励趋于上升；4) 在伯特兰竞争下这些发现基本成立；5) 当议价能力共享时，无论是否征收碳关税，技术转移都不会发生。

detail.abstract: The Serbia genocide, commonly known as the Bosnian genocide or Srebrenica massacre, is considered one of the heinous vestiges of ethnic cleansing and genocidal acts led by the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS) and Scorpions paramilitary group. Srebrenica, a small town in eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina, has become notorious as the site of one of the worst atrocities in Europe since World War II, which took place in July 1995 during the Bosnian war between 1992 and 1995. By the way, in the Bosnian case of genocide, it is discerned that geopolitics played a crucial role in which NATO and the West were wholly against the Bosnian Serbs since they broke international law and repudiated the decisions of NATO for maintaining a no-fly zone in Bosnia, while Russia has been in a shrewd stance due to their identical similarities and geopolitical interests of thwarting the influence of the West. Over the years, Serbia has been maintaining a strong alliance with Russia. However, Aleksandar Vucic, the president of Serbia is strategically hedging between both the West–NATO and EU– and Russia, retaining a close rapport with Moscow, at the same time, gradually improving its ties with the West. On one side, Vučić claims to have a genuine interest in joining the EU and encouraging regional integration via schemes like ‘Open Balkan’, on the other hand, the country continues to reject calls from the West for imposing sanctions against Russia and cutting ties with the country. Despite its pro-Russian leanings, this Balkan nation claims neutrality in the Ukraine war and promises to join the EU.

detail.title: Regulating Competition in African Digital Markets: From Form to Substance

declarations.funderStatement: This research was funded by a junior scholar grant received from the Economic Security Project.

keywords: South African Online Intermediation Platforms Market Inquiry

detail.abstract: Since the 1980s, many African countries began to adopt competition laws alongside structural adjustment and trade liberalization measures, selectively borrowing from existing EU and US regimes. Today, in response to global consolidation in digital markets, African governments are embracing sectoral regulatory schemes that have pro-competitive aims but go beyond traditional competition law. The structure and goals of the EU’s Digital Markets Act (DMA) are now being reflected in national and regional African frameworks such as the AfCFTA Protocol, South Africa’s Online Intermediation Platforms Market Inquiry and Kenya’s Competition (Amendment) Bill of 2024. The proliferation of these pro-competitive regimes in the African region even in the face of emerging trade barriers leads to two principal lessons. First, there seems to be an important alignment of interests between the EU and African jurisdictions vis-à-vis US tech giants. Reining in the power of US tech companies seems a fertile terrain of convergence and a priority in both regions. Second, despite the many limits of African competition authorities’ enforcement capabilities, pro-competitive regimes illustrate a hopeful appetite for an enforcement approach to tech markets that is not antithetic to traditional economic development rationales and yet that leaves space for local and regional African values.

affiliations: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad and Shiv Nadar University

detail.title: Age at Marriage and Women' s Labor Market Outcomes in India
detail.abstract: We examine the relationship between women's age at marriage and their labor market outcomes using nationally representative household data from India. Employing an instrumental variables-based empirical strategy, we find that a delay in women's age at marriage has no significant causal effect on their labor market outcomes. This is despite marriage delay being associated with higher education, lower fertility, and (possibly) higher dowry for Indian women. We argue that this might be because, older brides, as compared to younger brides, face more backlash from their partners. This backlash effect could be offsetting the positive labor market effects of marriage delay.

publicationDetails.detailsText: American Journal of International Law, Vol. 119, No. 4 (2025) (Forthcoming)

detail.abstract:
This essay focuses on the United States’ practices that rise from two executive orders—and their amendments—relating to foreign aid and reciprocal tariffs in the first six months of President Donald J. Trump’s second administration. The two executive orders are examined together because of their mutually reinforcing nature and illustrations of the unequal underbelly of our international development and economic orders. These executive orders have critical distributive implications for the Third World. President Trump’s actions continue his unrepentant focus on altering the extant international legal and economic order especially as the United States’ hegemony has come under significant threat by China. 

Crucially, the first six months of Trump’s second administration has laid bare the disrupting impact of power politics over diplomacy, neglect of rules-based international order, and non-empirically backed unfair-trade relations. Tariffs are now selectively deployed as instruments of economic coercion and political cudgel. By weaponizing and globalizing the experiences of the United States, the Trump administration retrenches the experiences of most of the world and relegates them to the background. Emerging from these executive orders then is an attempt by the United States to reconstruct the international economic order in favor of a specific national political project: America First. 

For African countries, the foreign aid cuts and reciprocal tariff executive orders accentuate the deeply unequal, unfair, and unjust character of an international legal regime that often subjects the Third World to domination, subordination, and acute disadvantage. Importantly, the high reciprocal tariffs also undermine the Africa Growth and Opportunities Act (AGOA) which recently expired. Despite the expiration, participating African states are hopeful of a year extension sometime before the end of 2025. By situating these executive orders in the false promises of even-handedness of foreign aid regime and the international trading system, this essay analyses the destabilizing impacts of these measures on the U.S.–African foreign aid relations. With the full return of transaction, power, and conditionality-based U.S. international economic relations, African countries confront a tricky dilemma: somewhat new, but reveals the violent playbook of imperialism after a period of rupture.

declarations.funderStatement: This work was funded by a grant from the European Research Council (ERC 949465).

detail.abstract: A Nash equilibrium of a game in extensive form is a sequential equilibrium in mixed strategies if it can be approximated through equilibria of close-by games with slightly perturbed payoffs and small-probability behavioral types. We show that sequential equilibria in mixed strategies are equivalent to (i) weakly sequential equilibria (Reny, 1992), (ii) normal-form perfect equilibria (Selten, 1975) in games with generic payoffs, and (iii) purifiable Nash equilibria (Harsanyi, 1973). A corollary of our results is that extensive-form perfect equilibria are normal-form perfect equilibria in games with generic payoffs.

detail.title: Asymmetric Learning and the CEO Labor Market
detail.abstract: Many models of the CEO market build on the classic analyses of Lucas (1978) and Rosen (1982) characterized by full information, a limited role for firm-specific human capital, and efficient allocation of workers across jobs and firms. But empirical evidence is not consistent with this approach. We explore an alternative focused on asymmetry of information between an executive's prospective employer and other potential employers, and an important role for firm-specific human capital. We show that our model better captures findings in the empirical literature concerning the CEO labor market than both the full information and efficient assignment approach and alternative models based on asymmetric information and inefficiencies.

title: The Welfare Synergy of Bundling International Environmental Agreements with International Trade Treaties

detail.title: The Welfare Synergy of Bundling International Environmental Agreements with International Trade Treaties
detail.abstract: I examine whether linking environmental cooperation with international trade agreements improves the welfare of the participating countries and allows countries to move closer to free trade compared to trade-only agreements. The model is an infinitely repeated game with the threat of reversion to Nash equilibrium if an economy deviates from the cooperative agreement. I find that such a synergy exists in a symmetric two-country model with two goods, both emitting pollutants even when the externalities have local impact. I use a combination of analytic and numerical simulation analysis to derive conclusions.

title: How to Use the Sharpe Ratio
affiliations: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Cornell University - Operations Research & Industrial Engineering, Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority

detail.title: How to Use the Sharpe Ratio
detail.abstract: The Sharpe ratio is the most widely used measure of investment efficiency, yet its statistical inference is often conducted incorrectly. This paper reviews the pitfalls of naive Sharpe ratio analysis and provides a comprehensive framework for its proper use. We identify five main pitfalls: (a) the Normality assumption; (b) neglect of statistical significance and minimum sample length assessment; (c) insufficient test power; (d) confusion between classical p-values and the probability of the null hypothesis given the data; and (e) failure to correct for multiple testing. To address these issues, we survey and extend a set of methods, including the Probabilistic Sharpe Ratio (PSR), Minimum Track Record Length (MinTRL), the Sharpe ratio’s Observed Bayesian Tail-Area False Discovery Rate (oFDR), and the Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR). Monte Carlo experiments confirm that these corrections yield more reliable inference than traditional t-statistics and general-purpose multiple-testing adjustments. We further distinguish between familywise error rate (FWER), false discovery rate (FDR), and hybrid FWER-FDR frameworks, showing their respective suitability for academic versus industrial applications. The central conclusion is that the Sharpe ratio remains a valuable metric only when properly corrected; without these adjustments, it risks misleading researchers and practitioners alike.

title: Constitutionalising Algorithmic Enforcement
affiliations: Queen's University Belfast - School of Law

detail.title: Constitutionalising Algorithmic Enforcement

publicationDetails.detailsText: forthcoming in Paul Torremans (ed), Intellectual Property Law and Human Rights (Kluwer International)

detail.abstract: This chapter offers a clear, comparative map of algorithmic enforcement in the IP domain, with emphasis on copyright and trade marks online. In short, the chapter argues for a constitutional settlement for automated IP enforcement. It begins by defining the operational toolkit—fingerprinting, hashing, classifiers, watermarking, demotion and related workflows. It treats filters and ranking systems not as inevitable black boxes but as governable institutions subject to rights-first limits, measurable performance, and public oversight. It then traces the voluntary, judicial and legislative drivers of today’s regime across multiple jurisdictions, integrating doctrinal developments with empirical evidence and law-and-economics insights to explain how incentives, error costs and market structure shape enforcement in practice. It shows how co-regulatory architectures (from DSA audits and researcher access to Ofcom’s codes) can convert private ordering into verifiable due process: clear reasons, explainability, appeal and human review, standardised accuracy metrics, auditable logs, and secure external testing. The core of the chapter tests these systems against fundamental-rights standards—due process, freedom of information and expression, privacy/data protection, and the freedom to conduct a business—using a proportionality and fair-balance frame that travels across jurisdictions. It closes with a policy-ready blueprint of ‘digital due process’ safeguards designed to protect rights and preserve contestability while keeping enforcement effective at scale. It also advances an incentive-compatible proposal—an algorithmic safe harbour conditioned on verified compliance—so effectiveness at scale is rewarded only when safeguards are real. The destination is pragmatic rather than utopian: an enforcement ecosystem that protects IP, preserves contestability for users and creators, and holds platforms to public-law-like duties, with empirical evaluation and iterative correction built in.

title: Group Decision-Making for Medical AI Fairness: Integrating Consistency Control and Classification-Based Consensus

detail.title: Group Decision-Making for Medical AI Fairness: Integrating Consistency Control and Classification-Based Consensus
detail.abstract: As AI integration in healthcare accelerates, it brings the potential for transformative innovation in healthcare delivery and equity. However, it also poses significant social risks, including data privacy breaches, unemployment, industry monopolies, and algorithmic biases, all of which threaten fairness and trust in AI applications. To address these issues, this paper proposes a comprehensive group decision-making framework incorporating a conflict consistency and classification consensus-based opinion minimum adjustment model (CCOMAM) to resolve expert conflicts regarding medical AI fairness practices. First, experts are invited to identify biases and fairness practices in medical AI. Then, evidence correlation coefficients derived from belief functions are used to quantify conflicts among experts’ opinions, and a consistency index is constructed to identify divergence. Second, the improved K-means++ is incorporated to dynamically determine optimal clusters of fairness practices. Third, the CCOMAM optimizes experts’ preferences by modified genetic algorithm that integrates penalties for inconsistency and rewards for high consistency and high consensus. Fourth, a two-dimensional consensus analysis is performed through consistency-consensus-clustering mapping plots, which analyze the interaction between individual consistency and group consensus for each fairness practice. Finally, the practicality and robustness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a case study on prioritizing fairness practices in an AI system for breast cancer diagnosis, including detailed model analysis. The framework transforms abstract fairness principles into concrete implementation pathways through consistency-consensus analysis, enabling healthcare organizations to systematically deploy AI fairness practices while addressing algorithmic biases and building stakeholder trust.

title: IusSpace: A Twelve-Dimensional Framework for Mapping Legal Evolution and Understanding Implementation Gaps in Global Governance

detail.title: IusSpace: A Twelve-Dimensional Framework for Mapping Legal Evolution and Understanding Implementation Gaps in Global Governance

declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics Declaration This research did not require formal institutional ethics approval as it involves exclusively the analysis of publicly available legal documents, legislative records, and published government statistics. No human subjects were involved in this research, and no personal or confidential data were collected or analyzed. Ethical Considerations The following ethical principles guided this research: 1. Data Sources: All data analyzed come from public sources including: - Published legislative texts and constitutional documents - Government statistical reports - International organization databases (World Bank, World Justice Project) - Academic publications and public policy reports 2. Country Analysis: While the research evaluates legal systems across different countries, all assessments are based on objective institutional characteristics rather than cultural judgments. The WEIRD/Non-WEIRD classification follows established academic frameworks (Henrich, 2020) and is used analytically, not prescriptively. 3. Transparency: - All data and code are publicly available under MIT License - Limitations and uncertainties are explicitly acknowledged - AI assistance in mathematical modeling is disclosed 4. No Harm Principle: This research aims to improve understanding of legal implementation challenges to support more effective reforms that benefit affected populations. 5. Cultural Sensitivity: The framework recognizes diverse approaches to governance as equally valid adaptations to different contexts, rejecting hierarchical judgments about legal systems. Statement The author confirms that all research was conducted in accordance with academic ethical standards for comparative legal research and social science analysis.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces IusSpace, a twelve-dimensional mathematical framework that enables the systematic mapping and analysis of legal systems as points in continuous space. Drawing inspiration from Richard Dawkins' concept of morphological space in evolutionary biology, where all possible biological forms exist within a multidimensional continuum, IusSpace positions each legal system according to twelve fundamental constitutional and institutional characteristics. This spatial approach reveals that legal reforms can be understood as vectors through this space, with their implementation success predictable based on the distance traveled and the cultural terrain traversed. Through empirical analysis of eighteen major legal reforms across thirteen countries between 2015 and 2024, we document a striking discovery: the world's legal systems cluster into two distinct regions of IusSpace based on their cultural characteristics, specifically whether they belong to WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic) or Non-WEIRD societies. These two regions exhibit fundamentally different properties regarding how legal reforms propagate through the space. Non-WEIRD societies, which encompass approximately 85% of the global population, show systematic implementation gaps averaging 31.2% between formal legal passage and actual implementation, compared to just 5.4% in WEIRD societies. This difference is statistically significant at p < 0.0001 with an effect size of Cohen's d = 3.749, representing one of the largest documented effects in comparative legal studies. The traditional Latin American concept of "se acata pero no se cumple" (one obeys but does not comply) emerges through this analysis not as a regional peculiarity or dysfunction, but as the dominant global pattern of legal adaptation. The framework achieves 87.4% accuracy in predicting implementation outcomes based solely on the geometric properties of reforms in IusSpace and the cultural characteristics of the implementing society. We provide open-source Python implementation of the framework and invite collaborative refinement of this foundational approach to understanding legal evolution.

title: Return on AI: A Decision Framework for Customers, Firms, and Society
affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology - Scheller College of Business, Texas A&M University - Department of Marketing and University of Notre Dame - Department of Marketing

detail.title: Return on AI: A Decision Framework for Customers, Firms, and Society
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving faster than firms' ability to measure its impact. In this paper, we introduce Return on AI (RoAI), a decision framework that forces clarity on how AI creates value and what it truly costs. RoAI begins by defining and situating AI investments relative to prior technologies, highlighting both their similarities and their distinctive risks. The framework requires managers to declare objectives and horizons in advance, measure benefits against a no-AI counterfactual, and make normalization choices explicit. Its numerator includes traditional sources of value-revenue lift, cost relief, and risk reduction, alongside dynamic mechanisms such as synergies, scale economies, network effects, and option value. Its denominator records the full set of costs: investment, change, operating, and learning. This structure exposes the biases that inflate pilots and distort scale-up decisions. RoAI is applicable across a wide range of industries. Startups may emphasize AI's signaling and option value, while established firms are more likely to focus on compliance, resilience, and productivity. We also extend the framework to a Societal RoAI that incorporates externalities for customers, workers, communities, and the environment. Crucially, we position RoAI not as a retrospective accounting device but as a catalyst for more scientific experimentation and pilots. Our aim is to encourage managers and researchers to design forward-looking pilots that can be measured credibly, reassessed systematically, and refined over time. Without disciplined thresholds and clear Go/No-Go criteria, firms risk mistaking hype for returns. With RoAI, they gain a common calculus for adopting AI responsibly and competitively, before the opportunity to shape AI's trajectory closes.

title: Towards Pseudonymous Undercollateralized Loans
affiliations: University of Tennessee, Knoxville, Haslam College of Business

detail.title: Towards Pseudonymous Undercollateralized Loans
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a design where defaulting borrowers lose access to undercollateralized loans temporarily. I show that under reasonable parameters, always-honest, i.e., paying back the loan, is the dominant strategy. The design works because borrowers are incentivized to keep their access to undercollateralized loans to avoid costly overcollateralized loans and the option to default. My design thus enables trust-minimized undercollateralized lending, increasing access and liquidity of DeFi protocols. The result is robust to practical considerations such as non-zero delinquency rate, autocorrelated returns, volatility clustering, moral hazard, and impatient borrowers. Importantly, even if borrowers are myopic and the mechanism fails, the structure enables a novel, trust-minimized option market.

title: The Joint Determination of Later Life Health and Educational Outcomes by Early Life Conditions: A Multinomial Logit Analysis
affiliations: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

detail.title: The Joint Determination of Later Life Health and Educational Outcomes by Early Life Conditions: A Multinomial Logit Analysis
detail.abstract: Literature documents strong evidence of connections between early life health and later life health and education outcomes while the outcomes are studied disjointedly. However, the associations between health and education outcomes in later life warrant those to be studied simultaneously. This article addresses the above concerns by applying Multinomial Logit model. Using Young Lives Survey (YLS) data, results indicate that good health at the average age of 0.5 years increases the probability of good health and poor educational performance by at least 9 percent and decreases the probability of poor health and good educational performance by at least 6.5 percent.

AI.tldr: 该研究使用多项式Logit模型分析早期健康与后期健康和教育成果的关联，发现0.5岁时的良好健康会增加后期良好健康但教育表现差的概率至少9%，减少后期健康差但教育表现好的概率至少6.5%。
AI.research_question: 早期健康如何同时影响后期健康和教育成果？
AI.motivation: 现有文献将健康和教育成果分开研究，但两者在后期生活中的关联性需要同时研究。
AI.theoretical_framework: 早期健康与后期发展关系的理论框架
AI.method: 使用多项式Logit模型分析Young Lives Survey数据

title: The Right to Explanation: Legal Challenges and the Future of Fairness in Automated Decision-Making
affiliations: Maastricht University - Faculty of Law and Independent

detail.title: The Right to Explanation: Legal Challenges and the Future of Fairness in Automated Decision-Making
detail.abstract: This article examines the legal foundations, scope, and practical challenges of the emerging "Right to Explanation" (RTE) in the European Union's regulatory framework on Artificial Intelligence (AI). It analyses the cognitive barriers inherent to Automated Decision-Making (ADM) systems-such as opacity, correlation-based logic, and bias-and assesses how the RTE can enhance transparency and fairness. The paper then offers a critical reading of Article 86 of the AI Act, highlighting both its innovative potential and its structural weaknesses, particularly concerning enforceability and accountability. It argues for a tailored, contextsensitive implementation of the RTE to ensure that it can meaningfully safeguard fundamental rights in the digital age.

AI.tldr: 本文分析了欧盟人工智能监管框架中新兴的"解释权"的法律基础、范围和实践挑战，评估了其如何增强透明度和公平性，并对《人工智能法案》第86条进行了批判性解读，主张采用量身定制的情境敏感实施方法。

AI.motivation: 随着自动化决策系统在欧盟的广泛应用，其固有的认知障碍（如不透明性、基于相关性的逻辑和偏见）对透明度和公平性构成挑战，需要建立有效的解释权机制。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于欧盟人工智能监管框架，特别是《人工智能法案》第86条关于解释权的规定，结合自动化决策系统的认知障碍理论。
AI.method: 法律分析和批判性解读方法，分析欧盟人工智能监管框架中的法律基础和结构性弱点。

title: The Price Level in a General Equilibrium Valuation Framework

detail.title: The Price Level in a General Equilibrium Valuation Framework

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.

keywords: Fiscal Theory of the Price Level

detail.abstract: This paper develops a continuous-time general equilibrium framework where the price level is determined by the valuation of the economy's real productive capacity. In our model, the price level equilibrates the real value of the total nominal base (the sovereign-issued unit of account) with the present value of the future consumption stream, priced via a stochastic discount factor. This general asset pricing approach provides a foundation where familiar relationships, such as the Fisher equation, emerge as no-arbitrage conditions, and concepts like the velocity of money are endogenously determined by the economy-wide valuation ratio. The framework clarifies how monetary and fiscal policies transmit to the price level through their influence on the pricing of risk and time, offering a unified lens to interpret diverse and puzzling inflation dynamics.

AI.tldr: 本文建立了一个连续时间一般均衡框架，通过经济实际生产能力估值确定价格水平。价格水平使总名义基础（主权发行的记账单位）的实际价值与通过随机贴现因子定价的未来消费流现值相等。

AI.method: 理论建模方法，构建连续时间一般均衡模型，运用随机贴现因子和资产定价理论。

title: What we Should Know about the Reliability of Empirical Legal Studies
affiliations: Boston University - School of Law

detail.title: What we Should Know about the Reliability of Empirical Legal Studies

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I currently serve as an Editor-in-Chief of MetaROR, a publish-review-curate platform.
declarations.funderStatement: This project was supported only by general research funds from Boston University.

detail.abstract: In September, 2012, Daniel Kahneman published an open email to psychology researchers studying priming effects. Kahneman was responding in part to reports that results from a number of priming studies that were widely cited, including in Kahneman’s 2011 book “Thinking Fast and Slow,” failed to replicate. Issuing a call to action, he encouraged the field to form an association that would lead a systematic effort to examine the replicability of priming results using credible methods. The email’s purpose was clear: to spur collective, quick, and transparent action to restore the field’s flagging credibility. During the past decade, metaresearchers across a wide range of disciplines have been systematically studying research processes employed in their fields, including research and reporting methods; incentives to produce research; how research is funded, reviewed and communicated; research misconduct; reproducibility; and the effects of reforms to research processes. The goal is to improve the credibility and production efficiency of scientific research. The findings of replication studies conducted in the early 2010s led many to declare that science was in the midst of a “replication crisis.” Since then, a growing number of reforms have been proposed and tested. The field of empirical legal studies seems behind other fields such as psychology, economics, political science, medicine, biology, and others that have taken significant steps toward uncovering the general reliability of the field’s empirical work, investigating the causes of observed unreliability, and instituting and testing the effects of various reforms. The purpose of this Article is to summarize what we know about the reliability of empirical legal studies and to highlight what, exactly, would be useful to learn. Part I summarizes, in broadbrush terms, what we know about the reliability of empirical research in fields other than empirical legal studies. Many fields are thought to be plagued by replication crises characterized by low rates of successful replication of randomly drawn samples of studies. These findings have set off alarm bells. They have also led researchers to explore what causes replication failures. Some of the causes are individual researcher-based while others are grounded in the scientific ecosystem. Part I also describes approaches used across fields to increase reliability and what we’ve learned about the efficacy of those approaches. Part II summarizes what we know about the general reliability of empirical legal studies. While the body of metaresearch focusing on the field is growing, it is relatively new. Overall, we know very little about the general reliability of ELS. Part III sets out a metaresearch agenda for the field. It outlines several important metaresearch questions about ELS that we do not yet have answers to but should. Part IV concludes.

AI.tldr: 本文总结了实证法律研究的可靠性现状，提出了该领域的元研究议程，旨在推动实证法律研究像其他学科一样进行系统性改革以应对复制危机。

AI.method: 文献综述和系统性分析，总结其他学科的元研究发现，评估实证法律研究现状，提出具体的研究议程。

title: AI Industrial Policy and Entrepreneurial Dynamics: Evidence from China's Pilot Zones
affiliations: Duke University

detail.title: AI Industrial Policy and Entrepreneurial Dynamics: Evidence from China's Pilot Zones
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first systematic evidence on the macroeconomic effects of AI-specific industrial policy. Exploiting the staggered rollout of China's AI pilot zones as a quasi-natural experiment, we construct comprehensive city-level measures of AI development and examine their impact on entrepreneurial dynamics. We find that the policy significantly increased firm entry rates, primarily by fostering local AI growth and generating technological spillovers that lowered entry barriers across industries. At a broader level, the policy promotes industrial upgrading by shifting activity toward manufacturing and services. Our findings highlight AI's role as a general-purpose technology whose policy-driven development can catalyze entrepreneurship and structural transformation, offering timely insights for the design of national AI strategies.

AI.tldr: 本文首次系统研究了AI产业政策的宏观经济效应，利用中国AI试点区的交错实施作为准自然实验，发现该政策显著提高了企业进入率，主要通过促进本地AI发展和产生技术溢出效应来降低各行业进入壁垒，推动产业升级。

AI.method: 利用中国AI试点区的交错实施作为准自然实验，构建城市级AI发展指标，考察其对创业动态的影响。

title: The importance of being many: dynamics, interactions and aggregation in a multi-sector economy
affiliations: Ca Foscari University of Venice - Dipartimento di Economia, Università degli Studi di Genova - DIME - Department of Mechanics, Energetics, Management and Transportation and University of Genoa

detail.title: The importance of being many: dynamics, interactions and aggregation in a multi-sector economy
detail.abstract: We examine how agent heterogeneity and interaction structures influence macroeconomic dynamics, challenging equilibrium frameworks based on aggregated-agent descriptions. Building on multi-sector models with numerous firms and households, we conduct analytical and computational comparisons between aggregated and disaggregated representations across different dynamical regimes. We identify precise conditions under which aggregated‐agent representations replicate multi-agent dynamics, and demonstrate their failure when shocks trigger structural regime shifts. Our analysis reveals that errors in aggregated‑agent frameworks escalate with: (i) heterogeneity, (ii) interaction asymmetries, and (iii) shock-induced network reconfigurations; we also quantify errors due to treating shock responses as equilibrium sequences rather than considering out-of-equilibrium dynamics.

AI.tldr: 本文通过多部门模型分析代理人异质性和互动结构对宏观经济动态的影响，挑战基于聚合代理人描述的均衡框架，发现聚合代理人表示在多代理人动态复制方面存在局限性，特别是在冲击引发结构体制转换时。

title: Can Sustainable Finance Save the Planet?
affiliations: Copenhagen Business School - Department of Finance

detail.title: Can Sustainable Finance Save the Planet?
detail.abstract:
This paper studies whether sustainable finance can mitigate climate change via its effect on firms' costs of capital, drawing on a rapidly growing literature. In theory, firms' discount rates would have to increase with their emission-to-value ratios, at a slope equal to the social cost of carbon ($43-$300 per ton). Empirically, the slope is only about $4, suggesting that sustainable finance is currently too weak to deliver a net-zero transition. Studying broader challenges, I show that discount rates should reflect all externalities weighted by their untaxed social costs, yet observed variation appears to be driven by investors' reliance on ESG scores with tenuous links to true social costs.

Journal of Finance: Insights and Perspectives, forthcoming
Symposium on Climate and Nature Finance, June 2026

title: To Acquire or to Ally? Foreign Competition and Firm Boundary
affiliations: University of Bath, School of Management, Durham University,  and University of Bath

detail.title: To Acquire or to Ally? Foreign Competition and Firm Boundary
detail.abstract: This study examines how foreign competition influences firms’ external growth strategies. Exploiting staggered U.S. import tariff reductions as a quasi-natural experiment, we find that heightened competition drives firms’ preferences toward forming strategic alliances. This shift is more pronounced for firms with limited financial or operational flexibility, weaker competitive positions, and those operating in low-entry-barrier industries. Under competitive pressure, firms preferentially form alliances with partners in the same industry as well as in high-tech, businessto-consumer (B2C), and product-differentiated sectors. In the long term, alliance-focused firms exhibit higher R&D intensity and patent outputs. Overall, the study highlights how domestic firms reshape external growth choices, partner selection, and long-term innovation outcomes in response to global competition shocks.

AI.tldr: 本研究探讨了外国竞争如何影响企业的外部增长战略。利用美国进口关税分阶段降低作为准自然实验，发现竞争加剧促使企业更倾向于建立战略联盟。这种转变在财务或运营灵活性有限、竞争地位较弱以及进入壁垒较低行业的企业中更为明显。在竞争压力下，企业优先与同行业以及高科技、B2C和产品差异化领域的合作伙伴建立联盟。长期来看，以联盟为重点的企业表现出更高的研发强度和专利产出。
AI.research_question: 外国竞争如何影响企业的外部增长战略选择？
AI.motivation: 随着全球化进程加快，企业面临日益激烈的外国竞争，需要了解这种竞争如何影响企业的战略决策，特别是外部增长方式的选择。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于资源基础观和竞争战略理论，探讨企业在竞争压力下的战略联盟选择行为。
AI.method: 利用美国进口关税分阶段降低作为准自然实验，采用实证分析方法检验外国竞争对企业战略联盟偏好的影响。
AI.findings: 1. 竞争加剧促使企业更倾向于建立战略联盟；2. 这种效应在财务/运营灵活性有限、竞争地位较弱、低进入壁垒行业的企业中更明显；3. 企业偏好与同行业、高科技、B2C和产品差异化领域的伙伴联盟；4. 联盟导向企业在长期具有更高研发强度和专利产出。
AI.theory_contributions: 丰富了竞争环境下企业战略选择理论，揭示了外国竞争如何重塑企业外部增长战略和伙伴选择模式。
AI.practical_contributions: 为企业管理者在全球化竞争背景下制定有效的联盟战略提供指导，帮助企业在竞争压力下优化外部增长决策。

title: P-Bubbles, Q-Bubbles, and Risk Premia
affiliations: Cornell University - Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management and The University of Sydney

detail.title: P-Bubbles, Q-Bubbles, and Risk Premia
detail.abstract: We develop a modeling framework that connects two distinct types of bubbles de ned in the literature: the rational bubbles (aka P-bubbles), and the local martingale bubbles (aka Q-bubbles). We relate both types of bubbles to an equity s risk premium via a novel decomposition. We empirically study this decomposition using a sample of stocks and ETFs, and nd that both types of bubbles are economically signi cant and important in understanding equity risk premium.

AI.tldr: 该论文开发了一个连接理性泡沫（P-泡沫）和局部鞅泡沫（Q-泡沫）的建模框架，通过新的分解方法将两种泡沫与股票风险溢价联系起来，并实证研究发现两种泡沫在经济上都具有显著重要性。

title: How Informative Are Acquirer Announcement Returns? Evidence from Merger Waves
affiliations: York University - Schulich School of Business and Université Laval - Département de Finance et Assurance

detail.title: How Informative Are Acquirer Announcement Returns? Evidence from Merger Waves
detail.abstract: We examine the informativeness of acquirer announcement-period cumulative abnormal returns (CARs) by classifying information revealed by the acquisition announcement into two types: the easy-to-process “tangible” information such as deal characteristics, and the hard-to-process “intangible” information such as acquirer misvaluation. We hypothesize that investors with limited cognitive capacity are unable to process intangible information over a short announcement window, leaving it to be reflected in stock prices only over a prolonged period. Consequently, short-term announcement returns are poor indications of long-term value creation. Analyzing a sample of deals categorized by industry merger waves, we identify acquirer overvaluation as a critical intangible factor affecting long-term performance. Our evidence reveals that short-term acquirer returns largely reflect tangible information while deeper valuation effects take years to influence stock prices. Our results highlight the limited utility of short-term announcement returns in assessing acquisition value.

title: Climate Regulation and Civil Society Activism
affiliations: University of Lille, Université Clermont Auvergne and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Climate Regulation and Civil Society Activism
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how public climate regulation shapes NGO activism against firms. Using monthly data on NGO campaigns across 78 countries (2010–2023), we find that the enactment of executive regulations significantly increases firm-targeted climate activism. Event-study estimates show no anticipatory trends and reveal a persistent, rising response. Consistent with our framework, the impact of regulation is larger in weaker enforcement environments and among nationally oriented NGOs with the capacity to act on domestic institutions. Public regulation thus mobilizes civil society as an informal enforcement layer, extending climate governance beyond formal state action.

title: Precautionary Saving Behavior in the Presence of Loss Aversion
affiliations: University of Leicester, Ashoka University and Lancaster University - Lancaster University Management School

detail.title: Precautionary Saving Behavior in the Presence of Loss Aversion
detail.abstract: We examine theoretically and experimentally, the relation between loss aversion and precautionary savings in a simple, two-period, consumption-savings model with future income uncertainty. Using an incentivized design, we elicit individual saving decisions and measure subject-specific loss aversion parameters. Our results show that loss aversion is associated with a lower likelihood of precautionary saving and reduced overall saving levels. Loss averse individuals overweight current consumption losses, associated with higher current savings, more than the insurance against future uncertain income losses. Asymmetric shocks reduce savings more than symmetric shocks because loss aversion magnifies the downside risk.

AI.research_question: 损失厌恶与预防性储蓄之间的关系是什么？

title: Designing MEMME – a conceptual Material and Energy Metabolism Model for Economies
affiliations: University of Lisbon - Instituto Superior Técnico, Alpen Adria University - Institute of Social Ecology and MARETEC—Marine, Environment and Technology Center,LARSyS, Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa

detail.title: Designing MEMME – a conceptual Material and Energy Metabolism Model for Economies
detail.abstract: Energy and materials drive the socioeconomic processes of the economy, acquiring economic value through physical and chemical transformations. Consequently, understanding an economy requires analyzing not only its monetary flows but also its biophysical flows and stocks. However, integrating material and energy perspectives into a unified analytical framework remains a challenge that existing approaches have only partially addressed. This study introduces the Material and Energy Metabolism Model for Economies (MEMME), a new conceptual biophysical model that provides a consistent and balanced accounting in both mass and energy units. MEMME focuses on material, energy, and food and feed transformations, integrating stocks and flows, to enable a more comprehensive analysis of social metabolism. It presents new indicators that improve our understanding of resource use, transformation efficiency, and their connection to economic activity, including a biophysical economic productivity indicator (BioEP), which measures how effectively physical outputs (materials and useful exergy) contribute to generating economic output. The Portuguese case study (1970-2022) shows that resource use increased with population and stock growth, while efficiency gains were modest. The shift from an Industry-based to a Services-based economy improved transformation efficiencies but did not reduce overall consumption. BioEP reveals that the Industry-based economy converted biophysical outputs into economic value more effectively than the Services-based economy. This highlights a trade-off between efficiency and productivity. Thus, absolute decoupling of resource use from economic growth appears unlikely. MEMME provides a consistent framework to derive such integrated insights.

AI.tldr: 本研究提出了物质与能源代谢模型（MEMME），这是一个统一的生物物理模型，用于分析经济体的物质和能源流动。通过葡萄牙案例研究（1970-2022）发现，资源使用随人口和存量增长而增加，效率提升有限，从工业经济向服务经济的转型提高了转化效率但未减少总体消费，且工业经济在将生物物理产出转化为经济价值方面更有效。
AI.research_question: 如何将物质和能源视角整合到一个统一的分析框架中，以更全面地理解社会经济代谢？
AI.motivation: 现有方法仅部分解决了将物质和能源视角整合到统一分析框架中的挑战，而理解经济不仅需要分析货币流动，还需要分析生物物理流动和存量。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于社会代谢理论，强调经济过程由能源和物质驱动，通过物理和化学转化获得经济价值。
AI.method: 开发了物质与能源代谢模型（MEMME），这是一个新的概念性生物物理模型，提供质量和能量单位的一致平衡核算，重点关注物质、能源以及食品和饲料的转化，整合存量和流动。
AI.findings: 葡萄牙案例研究表明：资源使用随人口和存量增长而增加；效率提升有限；从工业经济向服务经济的转型提高了转化效率但未减少总体消费；工业经济在将生物物理产出转化为经济价值方面比服务经济更有效。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了MEMME模型，提供了一个一致的分析框架，整合了物质和能源视角；引入了新的指标，包括生物物理经济生产力指标（BioEP），改进了对资源使用、转化效率及其与经济活动联系的理解。
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者提供了分析工具，以评估资源使用效率和经济生产力之间的关系；揭示了效率与生产力之间的权衡，表明资源使用与经济增长的绝对脱钩似乎不太可能。

title: Interactions Between Multiple Environmental Markets: Addressing Contamination Bias in Overlapping Policies
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Sussex

detail.title: Interactions Between Multiple Environmental Markets: Addressing Contamination Bias in Overlapping Policies
detail.abstract: To address the dual environmental challenges of pollution and climate change, China has established multiple environmental markets, including pollution emissions trading, carbon emissions trading, energy-use rights trading, and green electricity trading. Previous empirical studies suffer from known biases arising from time-varying treatment and multiple treatments. To address these limitations, this study adopts a dynamic control group design and combines Difference-in-Difference (DiD) and Artificial Counterfactual (ArCo) empirical strategies. Using panel data on A-share listed companies from 2000 to 2024, this study investigates the marginal effects and interactive impacts of multiple environmental markets implemented in staggered and overlapping phases. Existing pollution emissions trading mitigates the negative effects of carbon emission trading. Carbon trading suppresses (improves) financial performance (if implemented alongside energy-use rights trading). The addition of energy-use rights or green electricity trading in regions already covered by carbon or pollution markets has no significant effects.

AI.tldr: 本研究采用动态控制组设计和DiD-ArCo实证策略，分析中国多重环境市场（污染排放权交易、碳排放权交易、能源使用权交易、绿色电力交易）对A股上市公司的影响。发现现有污染排放权交易能缓解碳交易的负面影响，碳交易与能源使用权交易同时实施会抑制财务绩效，而在已有碳或污染市场中增加能源使用权或绿色电力交易无显著影响。
AI.research_question: 多重环境市场在交错和重叠实施阶段的边际效应和交互影响是什么？
AI.motivation: 解决现有实证研究中因时变处理和多重处理而产生的已知偏差，以更准确地评估中国多重环境市场的政策效果。
AI.theoretical_framework: 环境市场理论、政策评估理论、多重处理效应理论
AI.method: 动态控制组设计，结合差分法(DiD)和人工反事实(ArCo)实证策略，使用2000-2024年A股上市公司面板数据
AI.findings: 1. 现有污染排放权交易能缓解碳交易的负面影响；2. 碳交易与能源使用权交易同时实施会抑制财务绩效；3. 在已有碳或污染市场中增加能源使用权或绿色电力交易无显著影响
AI.theory_contributions: 发展了多重环境市场交互影响的理论框架，改进了时变处理和多重处理的实证方法
AI.practical_contributions: 为政策制定者提供多重环境市场协同实施的科学依据，帮助企业应对复杂环境政策环境
